correctness.rationale: The 32 distinct length-five factors force seven marks, since any position can hit at most five. Any seven-set is an attractor precisely when it hits all length-five windows and each of the thirty distinct short binary factors. The 120 possible window-hitting seven-sets follow from exact endpoint/gap inequalities. The supplied C++17 certificate enumerates all 2,048 anchored edge-simple Euler circuits and all 32 cuts, compares every candidate against all 30 short factor masks, and directly checks every nonempty factor for a seven-set witness in each of 65,536 cases. The verified extrema 30/120 and frequencies 4/22 follow from exhaustive multiplicity counting. The graph-to-cycle bijection supplies completeness beyond mere observed counts.

value.rationale: A paper explicitly raises how optimum attractors depend on general de Bruijn sequences. The first nonintegral binary five-window lower bound 32/5 creates a genuine short-factor coverage obstruction; showing that the lower ceiling seven is attained universally under every cut is stronger than the known special Lyndon sequence construction. Exact optimal-set multiplicities of 30 to 120 distinguish the richness of attaining witnesses, making this a meaningful complete natural classification rather than a recomputation of one table entry.
